text:
Alex: Quick Q — my spouse (on my plan) started receiving Medicare due to a disability last month. Can I keep them covered on Redwood during open enrollment or do we have to remove them? Any paperwork I should start gathering? :thinking:
Maria (People Ops): Hey @Alex — short answer: it depends. If they're on Medicare, our plan often ends up secondary for medical claims but you can usually keep them enrolled if they still meet dependent rules. We'll need documentation to properly coordinate.
Alex: Got it. Where do I upload docs, and will my payroll deductions change if they stay on the plan? Trying to avoid paying double for nothing.
BenefitsBot: KB: https://redwood.example.com/kb/benefits/medicare-coordination — lists typical docs required (Medicare card, SSDI award letter, Medicare entitlement notice) and timeline for reviews. :link:
Sam (Benefits): Hi Alex — to be clear: premiums are separate from claims coordination. We charge dependent premium unless eligibility ends or a QLE is processed. If you want us to review for premium adjustments or retro credits, upload the docs and we'll run a benefits coordination review.
Sam (Benefits): Quick steps:
1) Upload a photo or PDF of the Medicare card (front/back) + SSDI/Medicare entitlement notice.
2) Fill the short review form (Benefits > Manage Dependents or https://redwood.example.com/forms/medicare-dep-review).
3) We’ll confirm the effective date (usually end of the month after docs received) and whether any retro premium changes apply.
Alex: Thanks — uploaded the Medicare card and the entitlement letter to the portal and left a note "Alex / case 12345". If we keep both plans active, will providers get denied when they bill? Any guidance I should give clinics?
Maria (People Ops): Providers should bill Medicare first, then our plan as secondary. Sometimes that causes processing delays but not outright denials. Recommend giving providers both insurance cards and say "please bill Medicare primary." If a provider needs a claims coordination letter we can generate one after review.
Sam (Benefits): Also FYI: if the dependent is under 65 and on Medicare for disability, they may still meet dependent eligibility; turning 65 or changes in status triggers an update request. We'll email you a case number and next steps once review starts. :+1:
Alex: Appreciate it — pinged @Maria after upload. Thanks team!
